text.p: Profiles of Michael Johnson and Donovan Bailey who race over 150 metres on Sunday:

MICHAEL JOHNSON (U.S.), 29. First man to win Olympic 200 and 400 metres titles when he completed the double at last year's Atlanta Olympics. Clocked 19.32 seconds in the 200 to break his own world record set earlier in the year. Won 200 title at 1991 Tokyo world championships but eliminated in the semifinals at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics after suffering from food poisoning. Came back in the following year to win the 400 title at the Stuttgart world championships, then completed the 200-400 double at the 1995 Gothenburg world championships. Powerfully built sprinter with distinctive upright style who is unbeaten over 400 metres since February, 1989.

DONOVAN BAILEY (Canada), 29 - Jamaican-born, moved to Canada at the age of 13 and took up athletics in 1990. Won 100 title at 1995 Gothenburg world championships then set world record of 9.84 seconds in the Atlanta Olympic final. Followed up by anchoring Canada to victory over the United States in the 4x100 metres final.
